sections.domain: Traffic signs, route markers and sign colors
sections.heading: C — Traffic signs, route markers and sign colors
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic signs, route markers and sign colors

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
A sign's shape hints at its meaning, and the handbook teaches nine basic shapes to recognize. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
The eight-sided octagon means STOP, and the triangle means YIELD. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
A diamond shape marks a warning sign, and a five-sided pentagon marks a school sign. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
A pennant shape warns of a no-passing zone. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
A horizontal rectangle gives directions, while a vertical rectangle states a law. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
Both the round sign and the crossbuck mean a railroad crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A02
Route markers identify the federal, state and county road systems: interstate freeway, U.S. highway, state highway and county route signs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A02
Red on a sign means stop, prohibited or forbidden. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A02
Blue signs point to services and hospitality, and green signs give directions and guidance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A02
Yellow signs give caution or a general warning, while orange signals caution for construction or maintenance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A02
Black and white signs are regulatory, telling you what is legally allowed or prohibited. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A02
Fluorescent yellow-green warns of schools, pedestrians or bicycles, and fluorescent pink marks an incident, emergency or unplanned event. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A02
Brown signs point out places of recreation or cultural interest. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A02
Regulatory signs set specific laws on traffic speed and movement and are usually rectangles in white and black, red, white and black, or red and white. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A03
An Incident Ahead sign means an emergency or other unplanned event has disrupted traffic, and the signs that follow guide you around or through the area. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A03
A gas pump sign shows where gas stations are, and an Exit sign shows where the freeway exit is. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A03
Bridge Ices Before Road warns that a bridge may be icy even when the road is clear. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A03
A One Way sign means traffic in every lane moves in the same direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A03
A Speed Limit 50 sign sets the legal maximum on that stretch at 50 mph. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A03
A School Children Present sign means children are nearby, so drive carefully and follow a school crossing guard's directions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A03
A destination guide sign such as Brookfield and Onondaga tells you which way to go to reach those communities. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A03
A parking sign with a wheelchair symbol reserves the space for people with disabilities. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A03
A state route marker identifies a state highway, such as M-32. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A03
A parking permitted sign can limit the stay, such as two-hour parking between 8:30 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A03
At a stop sign, stop completely and yield to traffic and pedestrians before going on. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A03
At a yield sign, slow down and let vehicles crossing your path go first. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A03
No Turn On Red forbids turning on a red light, and separate signs prohibit right turns or U-turns. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A03
Lane-use signs show which lanes may turn left, and a Center Lane Left Turn Only sign reserves the middle lane for left turns. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A03
A Do Not Pass sign prohibits passing, and a Pass With Care sign on the right marks the end of that no-passing zone, so pass when safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A03
A Keep Left sign means traffic should go only to the left of a road feature or obstruction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A03
A Do Not Enter sign means you may not drive into that area. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A03
Authorized Vehicles Only marks a freeway emergency crossover reserved for police, emergency or maintenance vehicles; to reverse direction, exit and re-enter the freeway the other way. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A03
A Wrong Way sign means you have entered a lane of oncoming traffic and must get out as quickly and safely as possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F34 | anchor: A03
A No Trucks sign bars trucks from the posted area. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F35 | anchor: A03
The railroad crossbuck pictured in the sign challenge warns that a crossing made up of three tracks is ahead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F36 | anchor: A03
A Rest Area sign points to public restrooms, and a School Crossing sign warns of a crossing for children ahead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-F37 | anchor: A03
The orange slow-moving vehicle triangle is mounted on the back of vehicles that do not travel faster than 25 mph, such as Amish buggies and farm combines, so drive with care around them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0058]
